newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Telekom head says sell-off unlikely in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Turk Telekom head says sell-off unlikely in 1997.

text.p: The head of Turkey's state-run telecommunications company Turk Telekom said the first stage of the company's proposed privatisation would be possible in 1997, but was unlikely.
"In theory it is possible but it is difficult," Telekom general manager Cengiz Bulut told Reuters on Wednesday night.
A consortium led by Goldman Sachs was last month appointed to produce a Turk Telekom evaluation report. Bulut said it was expected to complete its report within seven months.

"A seven-month period fills the time until the middle of October. After that the assessment of Turk Telekom's value will be approved by the cabinet," Bulut said, adding that an adviser for the sell-off would then have to be selected.
Turkey is targeting revenues of $3.5 billion from the planned Turk Telekom sale. The sale of a 10 percent stake is envisaged for the last quarter of the year.

Earlier this year Turkey's constitutional court gave the green light for the sell-off, after having blocked it three times since 1993. The court ruled in favour of a law which allows for the sale of 49 percent of Turk Telekom's shares.
Under the law, a 34 percent stake is planned to be sold to domestic or foreign investors, 10 percent to the country's postal services and five percent to Turk Telekom employees.
Bulut said Turk Telekom was aiming to achieve a net profit of 100 trillion lira in 1997 after a profit of 50 trillion last year.
